newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel police chief warns of Arab violence.
newsitem.headline: Israel police chief warns of Arab violence.

text.p: Israel's police chief said on Sunday his forces feared construction of a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem could ignite Palestinian violence.
Asked if police shared the "fear and assessments" of other security forces about the prospect of violence over the project, Police Chief Assaf Hefetz told Israel Radio: "No doubt".

Palestinians have said Israel's plan to build 6,500 Jewish homes at Jabal Abu Ghneim, called Har Homa by Israel, violates peace deals and could lead to widespread unrest in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
"I think the problem...could be anywhere because of the concern that construction there could heat up the situation and lead to a deterioration in relations," Hefetz said.
Sixty-one Palestinians and 15 Israeli soldiers were killed in gun battles last September after Israel opened a new entrance to a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in East Jerusalem.
Justice Minister Tzachi Hanegbi warned in remarks broadcast on Sunday that Israel could oust Palestinian President Yasser Arafat from self-ruled Gaza Strip if violence erupted in the territories.

"Whoever launches violence could very quickly find himself packing a suitcase and travelling back and forth on the line from Tunis to Baghdad like he (Arafat) did for many years," Hanegbi told supporters on Saturday.

Israel says its peace deals with the PLO do not bar settlement construction in East Jerusalem, viewing all of the city as its capital. Palestinians claim East Jerusalem, occupied by Israel since 1967, as the capital of a future state.
